matches.note: R1 says syncPaymentMethod only sets the default card for PAUSED subscriptions, never resumes them, and the grace sweep then cancels them.
R5 sees that the save-card request swallows sync errors, but frames the problem as missing user feedback rather than a synchronous Stripe call with no durable retry or outbox.
No reported finding points out that retryable and permanent Stripe errors get the same handling.

unmatched_reported.note: Saving card A, then B, then A within 24h reuses the idempotency key, so Stripe returns the cached first response and the subscription stays on B.
A successful synchronous invoice payment leaves the local row delinquent until the webhook arrives, so a sweep that runs first can cancel a subscription the user just paid for.
Stripe leaves later invoices of an unpaid subscription in draft, so retrying only the latest invoice can skip the open invoice that is actually owed.
Already used as the partial match for F2 (swallowed sync errors in the save-card request).
Depends on role-gating behaviour inferred from other tests that the diff doesn't confirm; the trigger is speculative.
The cross-customer scenario is speculative and only asks to verify whether customers are shared.
Existing UNPAID rows still carry an old pastDueSince and become sweepable only after this change, so the first run cancels them immediately.
INCOMPLETE_EXPIRED rows are not skipped, so Stripe rejects the update and an error is logged on every card save.
